title: CI WorkflowTemplate builds glibc binary, not musl static — violates HR-1
description:

Running `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --bin claude-print` succeeds and produces a 1.1MB binary at the musl release output path; `ldd` on that binary reports "statically linked" (confirmed by direct test). So the fix is low-risk.

title: Add src/session.rs: Session::run() orchestration
description:
Create src/session.rs with a Session::run() function that orchestrates the full PTY pipeline. main.rs calls this; it owns nothing about CLI parsing or output formatting.

## What to implement

pub struct SessionResult {
    pub transcript: TranscriptResult,   // from transcript.rs
    pub claude_version: String,
    pub duration_ms: u64,
}

pub fn run(
    claude_bin: &Path,
    claude_args: &[OsString],      // flags to forward: --model, --max-turns, --settings <path>, optionally --setting-sources=
    prompt: Vec<u8>,
    timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
) -> Result<SessionResult>

Internally:
1. HookInstaller::new() — creates temp dir, hook.sh, stop.fifo
2. Resolve claude version: Command::new(claude_bin).arg("--version").output()
3. Build child argv: [claude_bin, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --settings <hook.settings_path>, ...claude_args]
4. Self-pipe for SIGINT: pipe2(O_CLOEXEC); install signal handler writing one byte to write-end
5. PtySpawner::spawn(cmd, args)
6. EventLoop::new(pty.master_fd, self_pipe_read)
7. TerminalEmu::new() — check terminal.rs for its API
8. StartupSeq::new(prompt) (or with_idle_gap if DEFAULT_POST_DISMISS_IDLE_MS needed)
9. Loop via event_loop.run(|chunk| { ... }):
   - Feed chunk to TerminalEmu; write any probe responses to master_fd
   - Feed chunk to StartupSeq.feed(); on Write(bytes) write to master_fd; on HardTimeout return Err
   - Call StartupSeq.poll_timers() each iteration; handle Write/HardTimeout
   - When StartupSeq.phase() == PromptInjected and FIFO not yet added: open_fifo_nonblock() and event_loop.add_fifo_fd()
10. Match ExitReason from event_loop.run():
    - FifoPayload(bytes): parse_stop_payload → resolve_stop_info → read_transcript()
    - ChildExited: Err(Error::NoResponse)
    - Interrupted: send SIGTERM to child, return Err(Error::Interrupted)
11. Handle timeout_secs: wrap the event loop in a thread or use SIGALRM; on expiry SIGTERM child and return Err(Error::Timeout)
12. PtySpawner::waitpid(); HookInstaller drops automatically

## Complete when
- src/session.rs compiles as part of the workspace (add pub mod session to lib.rs)
- Unit test test_session_runs_mock_claude: sets CLAUDE_BINARY=path/to/mock_claude, calls session::run() with a test prompt, asserts SessionResult.transcript.text is non-empty

title: Default hook inheritance broken: session.rs unconditionally forces --setting-sources=, making --no-inherit-hooks a no-op (HR-5 violation)
description:
Plan docs/plan/plan.md "Hard Requirements" #5: "MUST NOT break user hooks in default mode -- all hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json MUST fire alongside the relay hook." Also "Hook Inheritance and Log Placement > Default: Inherit User Hooks" section: by default claude-print must NOT pass --setting-sources= to the child; only "--no-inherit-hooks" (isolation mode) should do that.

ACTUAL BUG (verified by reading src/session.rs and src/main.rs): src/session.rs Session::run_inner() builds the child argv with this unconditional sequence (around line 218-223):
  args.push("--dangerously-skip-permissions")
  args.push("--settings=<temp>/settings.json")
  args.push("--setting-sources=")   <-- always pushed, no conditional
  for arg in claude_args { ... }
Separately, src/main.rs conditionally pushes "--setting-sources=" into claude_args only when cli.no_inherit_hooks is true (around line 125) -- but since session.rs already always adds it unconditionally one way or another, that conditional in main.rs is functionally meaningless: every single invocation of claude-print, whether or not --no-inherit-hooks was passed, results in --setting-sources= being forwarded to the child claude process.

CONSEQUENCE: the plan-documented "Default: Inherit User Hooks" mode (which is supposed to be the default, non-flagged behavior) does not exist in the current binary -- claude-print always runs in isolation mode. Users' ~/.claude/settings.json hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, ccdash, trail-boss, etc.) never fire for ANY invocation, not just NEEDLE-dispatched ones with --no-inherit-hooks. This is a live violation of Hard Requirement 5. tests/hooks.rs only exercises HookInstaller in isolation (checking settings.json/hook.sh file contents) -- it never asserts anything about the actual child argv assembled by session.rs, so this regression currently has zero test coverage and would not be caught by cargo test.

CONTEXT: the unconditional --setting-sources= push carries a comment in session.rs explaining it was added because "inheriting global hooks (SessionStart, etc.) can cause the child to hang at startup" -- this appears to be a deliberate but over-broad fix related to the still-open startup-wedge hardening bead bf-uj0 ("Make child claude startup non-blocking in headless mode... bound or disable MCP server initialization for headless runs"). This bead should NOT redo bf-uj0's investigation into why inheritance can hang -- it should only make the --setting-sources= forwarding conditional again (matching the plan and the --no-inherit-hooks flag) while leaving whatever narrower startup-safety fix bf-uj0 lands on intact. If reconciling the two truly requires a different mitigation (e.g. bounding MCP init instead of blanket source suppression), flag that as a note for bf-uj0 rather than blocking this bead on it.

FIX:
- Thread the no_inherit_hooks flag (or equivalent) into Session::run/run_inner, and only push the hardcoded "--setting-sources=" line when it is set. Remove the now-redundant duplicate push in main.rs (pick session.rs OR main.rs as the single source of truth for this flag, not both).
- Add an integration-level test asserting: (a) a default invocation (no --no-inherit-hooks) does NOT include --setting-sources= anywhere in the child argv (capture via a test seam in PtySpawner::spawn or by reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline per the plan's own "Hook Inheritance Tests" spec), and (b) --no-inherit-hooks DOES include it. This directly implements the plan Testing section "Hook Inheritance Tests (tests/hooks.rs) > --no-inherit-hooks flag" test that is currently missing.

title: Tail real transcript path in live stream-json reader (tails non-existent <temp>/transcript.jsonl)
description:
CONTEXT (premise correction — read first): The live stream-json reader is ALREADY wired into the production session path. src/session.rs (~line 549) spawns emitter::spawn_stream_json_reader at the PROMPT_INJECTED transition; src/emitter.rs has a complete StreamJsonHandle with Drop-based join (plan invariant INV-8), signal_drain, and the 50ms/5s file-open retry loop. The old replay function no longer exists (grep finds zero references). So do NOT re-implement the wiring — it is done and all 120 lib tests pass. This child and its siblings are about making the already-wired feature ACTUALLY WORK.

THE BUG (verified): src/session.rs (~line 475) sets transcript_path = temp_dir_path.join("transcript.jsonl") and hands that to the reader. But neither real claude nor mock_claude ever writes there — the transcript lands under ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl (mock_claude writes ~/.claude/projects/mock-cwd/<id>.jsonl; see test-fixtures/mock-claude/src/main.rs ~line 169). So the reader's file-open retry times out after 5s and forwards NOTHING. tests/stream_json_incremental.rs lines 22-27 document this as the core remaining bf-5vm work; running that test with --ignored confirms zero streamed lines. This is why the feature has not actually worked despite the wiring shipping.

THE HARD PART: the transcript path's session_id is assigned by claude and is only present in the Stop payload — which arrives AFTER PROMPT_INJECTED, where the reader is spawned. So the reader cannot be handed a final path at spawn time.

WORK: Make the reader tail the REAL transcript path. Recommended approach — at PROMPT_INJECTED, derive the projects dir from cwd (~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/) and have the reader DISCOVER this session's JSONL by scanning that dir for a .jsonl created since injection (newest matching file), reusing the existing 50ms/5s open-retry loop until it appears. Keep the start_offset capture (transcript file size at injection). Re-spawning only after Stop would forfeit live pre-Stop tailing — the entire point of bf-5vm — so prefer discovery over late-spawn.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Unit/integration test proving the reader tails the path mock_claude actually writes (~/.claude/projects/mock-cwd/<id>.jsonl), forwarding lines as the file grows. Extend the existing NON-ignored incremental reader unit test already present in tests/integration/scenarios.rs (the one that deterministically pins live-tail growth of the reader directly, independent of mock_claude) to use a projects-dir-style path.
- No regression: the 120 lib tests still pass.

title: EC-7 unimplemented: Stop firing before PROMPT_INJECTED is never detected (FIFO registered at session start, not at the PROMPT_INJECTED transition)
description:
Plan docs/plan/plan.md "State Machine > StartupSeq States" diagram: "Stop fires before PROMPT_INJECTED -> error: emit is_error=true, exit 2 (see EC-7: a response to an unsent prompt indicates a session identity leak)". Also "Event Loop > Dynamic fd registration": "The event loop initially polls only master_fd (1 fd). At the TRUST_DISMISSED -> PROMPT_INJECTED transition, the FIFO read-end fd is added to the poll() set." Also Edge Case Catalog EC-7, and the Testing > Mock PTY Integration Tests table row "Stop fires before PROMPT_INJECTED | MOCK_STOP_BEFORE_INJECT=1 | exit 2, is_error: true in output (EC-7 path)".

ACTUAL GAP (verified by reading src/session.rs and grepping the whole repo): session.rs Session::run_inner() opens the Stop FIFO and calls event_loop.add_fifo_fd(...) once, unconditionally, at session setup (step 9, BEFORE event_loop.run() is ever invoked) -- not dynamically at the TRUST_DISMISSED -> PROMPT_INJECTED transition as the plan specifies. There is no tracking anywhere of whether startup.phase() had reached PromptInjected at the moment a Stop payload arrives: the ExitReason::FifoPayload match arm processes any Stop payload unconditionally and returns it as a normal response. grep -rn "MOCK_STOP_BEFORE_INJECT|EC-7|phase() ==" src/ tests/ test-fixtures/ returns zero matches anywhere in the repo -- this safety check does not exist in any form, and the mock_claude fixture does not even support the MOCK_STOP_BEFORE_INJECT env var yet (explicitly called out as out-of-scope follow-up work in bead bf-3isy).

RISK CONTEXT: pty.rs already unsets CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID before execvp (EC-11 mitigation), which the plan states "should prevent this in normal operation" -- so EC-7 is a defense-in-depth backstop, not a currently-observed production failure mode. That is why this is filed at lower priority than the is_error/exit-1 and hook-inheritance bugs. But it is a concretely specified, testable, currently-absent safety behavior from the plan, not merely a doc gap.

FIX:
- In session.rs Session::run_inner(), when ExitReason::FifoPayload is received, check whether startup.phase().is_prompt_injected() was true at that point (this requires capturing the phase at the moment the event loop callback processes the FIFO, or checking startup.phase() immediately after event_loop.run() returns, since startup is owned by run_inner and not mutated by the FIFO branch itself). If the phase never reached PromptInjected, treat it as the EC-7 condition: return an error (is_error=true, exit 2) rather than proceeding to read_transcript() and returning Ok(...).
- Add a unit or session-level test for this that does not require a full mock_claude PTY round-trip: e.g. a lower-level test on the match logic itself, or (if convenient) extend test-fixtures/mock-claude to support MOCK_STOP_BEFORE_INJECT (coordinate with bf-3isy which explicitly deferred that env var) and add the plan-specified integration test scenario.
- cargo fmt / clippy / test clean per plan Definition of Done.

title: Large-prompt (>32KB) relay pastes literal $(< path) instead of prompt contents
description:
src/startup.rs:222-235 (make_file_relay_payload), reached from make_prompt_payload at src/startup.rs:208 when prompt.len() > INLINE_PROMPT_MAX (32 KB).

WHAT IS WRONG: For prompts larger than INLINE_PROMPT_MAX, the code writes the prompt to a temp file and injects the byte sequence `ESC[200~$(< <path>)ESC[201~CR` — i.e. a shell command-substitution expression wrapped in bracketed-paste markers. But bracketed paste delivers its payload to Claude Code's Ink REPL as LITERAL text (see plan.md glossary 'Bracketed paste': it only wraps text so embedded newlines don't trigger premature Enter; the content is inserted verbatim). There is no shell in the injection path to evaluate `$(< path)`. The model therefore receives the literal 11+N-byte string '$(< /tmp/....tmp)' as the prompt, never the file contents. Every prompt above 32 KB is silently delivered wrong (empty/garbage prompt), while claude-print still reports success.

This diverges from the plan's own claim (prompt.rs:11-14 and startup.rs:22-25) that >32 KB prompts are 'a legitimate, supported input (relayed to a temp file)'.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (code-level, verifier-confirmable): make_file_relay_payload must deliver the actual prompt bytes into the TUI input, not a shell substitution expression the REPL never evaluates. Objective check: the injected payload for a >INLINE_PROMPT_MAX prompt must not contain the literal substr '$(< '; instead it must carry the prompt content itself (e.g. chunked bracketed-paste writes of self.prompt). A unit test can assert the payload bytes contain the prompt content and do NOT contain b"$(< ".
